finding.claim: dropTable ignores the result of Authorize(u, "dba"), so any authenticated user can drop tables.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to /admin/drop (route registered at api.go:44); the caller needs only a *User in request context.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE ...") at api.go:27, a destructive DDL operation.

trace.note: userFrom(r) loads the user from request context.
Authorize(u, "dba") returns errors.New("forbidden") for non-dba users, but the return value is discarded.
Execution continues and runs the DROP TABLE regardless of the authorization result.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) has correct logic but its error is never checked. dropTable has no other role, method, or CSRF check. vacuum (api.go:33-36) checks the error correctly, which shows the intended pattern.

verdict.guard_found: none. Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error for non-dba users, but dropTable discards it as a bare statement at api.go:26. Nothing else in dropTable (api.go:24-29) or the route registration (api.go:44) checks the role before runSQL at api.go:27.
verdict.reason: dropTable at api.go:26 discards the error from Authorize(u, "dba") and runs runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 regardless, so any caller holding a *User in context, which the route at api.go:44 exposes, can drop tables.

finding.claim: The table name from the request is concatenated into a DDL statement with no validation, quoting or allowlist, enabling SQL injection and arbitrary destructive statements.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27, which reads from the query string or the form body.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27. runSQL (api.go:41) is a no-op stub here, so exploitability depends on its real implementation.

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") is read from attacker-controlled query or body.
The value is string-concatenated into the SQL text.
runSQL receives the string. In this file it is a stub; if it executes raw SQL, the injection is live.

finding.guards_checked: No identifier validation, table-name allowlist, QuoteIdentifier, or parameterization on this path. FormValue accepts GET query parameters, so the state change is reachable by GET (CSRF exposure once F1 is fixed, if cookies are ambient). Authorize is not checked, see F1.

verdict.guard_found: No identifier validation, table-name allowlist, QuoteIdentifier, or parameterization on the path. The only nearby control, Authorize at api.go:26, is a bare call whose error is discarded, so it does not block the request. The Authorize check in vacuum (api.go:33-36) is not on this path.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate: api.go:27 concatenates the unvalidated r.FormValue("t") into the statement, and api.go:41 is an empty stub `func runSQL(string) {}` that ignores its argument, so no SQL executes in this code. Whether this is SQL injection depends on the real runSQL implementation, which is not in the available files, so the injection claim cannot be decided from this code. The reachability is confirmed separately: the Authorize result at api.go:26 is discarded, so the handler runs for any authenticated user.

finding.claim: userFrom performs an unchecked type assertion on the request context, and no authentication middleware is visible in this file, so /admin/* handlers panic or run without a verified user unless the server wraps them elsewhere.
finding.source: The "user" context value, which is set outside this file. Requests to /admin/drop and /admin/vacuum reach the handlers directly (api.go:44-45).
finding.sink: Type assertion r.Context().Value("user").(*User) at api.go:22, used by the authorization decisions in dropTable and vacuum. A missing or wrong-typed value panics the request handler.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered directly with no wrapping middleware in this file.
/admin/vacuum is registered directly with no wrapping middleware in this file.
vacuum calls userFrom(r) before its authorization check.
The assertion .(*User) has no ok check. A missing or wrong-typed value panics. A typed-nil *User panics later at api.go:14 (u.Roles).

finding.guards_checked: No ok-form assertion and no nil check. No middleware is visible in this file. The context key is an untyped string ("user"), which go vet flags and which can collide with other packages. Unverified: where the "user" value is set and whether /admin/* is wrapped by authentication middleware. Confirm outside this directory.

verdict.guard_found: Inside api.go: no authentication middleware and no ok-form assertion or nil check at line 22. Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error, but dropTable (api.go:26) discards it as a bare statement, so it has no effect. vacuum (api.go:33-36) does check the error and returns 403. Outside this file: none visible. The code that sets the "user" context value and any wrapper on /admin/* are not in the directory.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (api.go:22, 25, 26, 32, 44, 45), but whether /admin/* is reachable without a verified user depends on code outside this directory, which only lists api.go. Within the file, the only confirmed defect is that dropTable ignores the Authorize result at api.go:26, so any request that does carry a user, including a low-privilege one, can reach the raw-concatenated DROP TABLE at api.go:27; that is a separate finding from the one claimed.
